How It Is JudgedRubrics

Every made thing is judged against a published rubric, and every course sits an unassisted examination against its own. Levels run beginning, developing, proficient, mastered.

  • The made response (the Canon)
  • The quantitative study (Mathematics and Science)
  • The working system (Computation and Engineering)
  • The writing portfolio (Rhetoric)
  • The forensic teardown (Epistemics)
  • The cultural artifact (Culture and Signal)
  • The shipped build (the Workshop)
  • The studio work (the Depths)
  • The field report (the Field Term)
  • The capstone (the defended original work)
  • The unassisted examination (every course)
What Happens With ItProgram review

The portfolio is the primary evidence. At each annual gate the faculty read every student's portfolio against the five outcomes and record a level for each. Each year the levels are aggregated by outcome and by course; a course whose students fall short on an outcome it claims is revised before the next year, and the revision is recorded with the reason. This is the program-review loop, and it is the same loop the gates run for each student.

Status

A working framework, not an authorized degree. SDIT is in its founding phase and is not yet authorized to grant degrees; where authorization stands is published in full. The curriculum is open and free to take.
